documented_concern: Every single audit reporting package for FY2016-FY2025 was accepted by the Federal Audit Clearinghouse after March 31 of the following year, the standard nine-month date. The delay was 12 days for FY2016, 99 days for FY2018, 64 days for FY2024 and 113 days for FY2025, and 290 days or more for FY2017 and FY2019-FY2023; the FY2021 package was accepted on 2025-01-14, about 42 months after year end.
page_or_section: FAC acceptance dates in table 11; 2 CFR 200.512(a)(1)
context_and_limits: The federal acceptance date can trail submission by some days. Federal COVID-19 guidance allowed extensions for fiscal years ending through June 30, 2021, so lateness against an extended date is not computed for FY2019-FY2021. The Director of Budget and Finance described the audit as performed "in a timely and collaborative manner" on 2025-07-28 (joint Finance Committee and Select Board minutes of that date, p. 3).
standard_note: Listed for follow-up. Not a finding of misconduct.

documented_concern: The auditor's summary in every reporting package for FY2016-FY2025 reports that the Town did not qualify as a low-risk auditee; the Federal Audit Clearinghouse records the same answer for all ten years.
page_or_section: Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs, Section I (Summary of Auditor's Results): PDF p. 10 (FY2016-FY2020), p. 13 (FY2021), p. 9 (FY2022), p. 95 (FY2023), p. 97 (FY2024 and FY2025); page list in table 11
context_and_limits: Low-risk status requires, among other conditions, timely filing in each of the two preceding audit periods (2 CFR 200.520(a)). Non-low-risk status increases required audit coverage; it is not itself a finding. The answers were read from the page images because the check marks do not survive text extraction.
standard_note: Listed for follow-up. Not a finding of misconduct.

category: Board of Public Works transition during FY2027 rate-setting
documented_concern: The Board of Public Works, which approved the FY2027 water, sewer and solid waste rates on July 22, 2026, was expanded from three to five members with effect from July 1, 2026 by a charter amendment (Fall 2025 Town Meeting Article 9, approved by voters on April 7, 2026). On August 3, 2026 the Town reported that the Board had two vacant seats and the Select Board appointed two members that day, after the rates had been approved; on August 31, 2026 the Select Board accepted one resignation from the Board and appointed a replacement. The Department of Public Works web page still described a three-person board on November 11, 2026.
